summary: Both r1 MEDIUM blockers are genuinely closed in the spec text and I verified each against the actual source. MED-1 (name-collision miscompile): §8 now mandates a BIDIRECTIONAL, order-independent cross-check and explicitly names the side a lazy implementer would skip — 'register_shared MUST be EXTENDED to reject a name already in the local-array map' — not just the easy register_local_array->shared direction. This is the correct fix: I confirmed register_shared (typecheck.rs:812-843) today checks only shared_name_map dup + find_param + find_binding and knows nothing about local arrays, so without the extension the collision would be one-directional and order-dependent. AT-2942 tests BOTH declaration orders. MED-2 (hoist-no-reset foot-gun): §5.1 rejects nested decls with a hard HIR error LocalArrayDeclNotAtBlockScope; I confirmed this is mechanically sound and cheap because typecheck already has two distinct statement-dispatch paths — a top-level loop (typecheck.rs:1197) and a separate nested-block loop (typecheck.rs:1795) — so the nested path can emit the scope error while the top-level path registers. AT-2943 covers for-body and if-body nesting plus proves top-level-decl-indexed-inside-loop still compiles. All four r1 LOWs applied and verified: corpus-wide golden (AT-2940, and I re-confirmed `array` appears in examples/ ONLY inside // comments — zero bare-identifier use, so inert by construction); token.rs not lib.rs (keyword_from_str at token.rs:256 next to "shared"=>Shared, exactly as the spec states); decidable const-OOB hard error with an EXACT boundary (index==N rejected, N-1 clean, symbolic exempt — AT-2944); path-insensitivity honestly disclosed in §5. Schema v3->v4 factual fix verified (CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION=4 at metadata.rs:194, test asserts M3.17 bump). LOC reconciliation (target 1600 / cap 2000) is honest and defensible — I verified the shared.rs anchors (hir 191, codegen 223) and the §12 math (optimistic-measured ~2745 comparable MINUS the ~700 barrier-hazard proof M3.20 provably omits = ~2045 cap). AT range AT-2927..AT-2944 is collision-free (grep confirms these appear only in M3.20 files; prior campaign tops at AT-2926; AT-2945 is only cited as the budget ceiling). Two NEW low-severity notes fall out of the r2 nested-decl-reject decision (cascade-suppression + dual-error-enum placement) — both are error-QUALITY, not correctness, and non-blocking. The design is sound and buildable; I APPROVE.
warnings: LOW (NEW, from the r2 nested-decl REJECT decision — cascade suppression unspecified): §5.1 rejects a nested `array` decl at HIR but is silent on whether the rejected name is still REGISTERED for the remainder of the block. If it is NOT registered, then `for { array a: array[f32,4]; a[j] = x; }` emits LocalArrayDeclNotAtBlockScope for the decl AND a cascade of LocalArrayUndeclared for every `a[j]` use in the block — multiple diagnostics for one root cause, which dilutes report-ALL (anti-pattern #6 wants all DISTINCT errors, not cascade noise). Note `shared` does not hit this today because a nested `shared` decl is currently ACCEPTED (no scope check), so it registers and later uses resolve. RECOMMENDATION (non-blocking, Coder's discretion): after emitting the scope error, still register the array (poisoned) so in-block uses resolve and do not cascade — emit the root error exactly once. State the chosen behavior and add it to AT-2943's expectation (exactly one LocalArrayDeclNotAtBlockScope, no LocalArrayUndeclared cascade).

LOW (NEW — dual error-enum placement imprecision): the spec labels the new errors `HirError::LocalArrayDeclNotAtBlockScope` / `HirError::LocalArrayConstIndexOutOfBounds` / `LocalArrayNameCollision` and lists them under validate.rs (§8), but the analogous `shared` variants exist in TWO enums — `TypecheckError` (typecheck.rs: SharedNameCollision:604, SharedDuplicateName:620, SharedZeroLength:628, ...) AND `validate::HirError` (validate.rs:172-287) — and the collision/scope/const-OOB checks the spec puts in `check_local_array_read`/`_write` and the lowering walk run inside typecheck, which emits `TypecheckError`, not `HirError` (see the live emit at typecheck.rs:827 `TypecheckError::SharedNameCollision`). So a faithful mirror must add each M3.20 variant to BOTH enums and emit the typecheck-phase ones as `TypecheckError::*`. Non-blocking (the shared mirror naturally guides this), but the spec's `HirError::` labels are misleading about which enum the typecheck-phase emits use; the Coder should reconcile. Minor LOC implication (variants duplicated across two enums) is within the 1600/2000 envelope.
spirv_concerns: CONFIRMED-OK (unchanged from r1, re-affirmed): Function-storage OpTypeArray of f16/u8 needs ONLY the element-type capability (Float16/Int8), never StorageBuffer8/16BitAccess or SPV_KHR_*_storage — those gate StorageBuffer/Uniform/PushConstant classes; Function (like Workgroup) is exempt. Proven by the working shared[f16] path. AT-2936 is the load-bearing guard and is retained.

CONFIRMED-OK: entry-block-prelude OpVariable placement is real and mandatory — body.rs already emits let-scalar Function OpVariables in the first-block prelude with a var-after-non-var assertion; the spec (§7, §9) correctly mandates the array OpVariable be inserted in that same prelude loop. No structured-control-flow violation.
vendor_concerns: Unchanged from r1: the 1024-byte spill advisory / 4096-byte hard cap are static heuristics (device register budget is not portably exposed); the spec acknowledges this (open_question, §6, §15 M3.12-analogy reframing). Acceptable; cap is un-tunable per-vendor until EB.1 hardware data. Note the 4KB cap is 16x tighter than shared's 64KB precisely because private memory is replicated per-thread — a sound conservatism.
missing_tests: SATISFIED: AT-2942 tests name-collision in BOTH declaration orders (guards the bidirectional §8 fix) — the #1 r1 blocker's test now exists.
SATISFIED: AT-2943 tests nested-decl rejection (for-body + if-body) AND proves top-level-decl-indexed-inside-loop compiles clean — the #2 r1 blocker's test now exists.
SATISFIED: AT-2940 strengthened to corpus-wide byte-identity (cross-branch), not just the 5 golden kernels.
SATISFIED: AT-2944 tests const-OOB write + read hard error, in-bounds clean, and symbolic-exempt.

SUGGESTED (non-blocking, ties to warning #1): extend AT-2943's expectation to assert EXACTLY ONE LocalArrayDeclNotAtBlockScope diagnostic with no LocalArrayUndeclared cascade for in-block uses of the rejected name.
questions_for_architect: Cascade suppression (non-blocking): when a nested `array` decl is rejected at HIR, is the name still registered (poisoned) so in-block uses resolve without a LocalArrayUndeclared cascade? Please state the behavior and reflect it in AT-2943 (warning #1). This is error-quality, not correctness — does not gate coding.

Enum placement (non-blocking): confirm the typecheck-phase errors (name-collision, nested-decl scope, const-OOB) are emitted as `TypecheckError::*` (mirroring SharedNameCollision at typecheck.rs:827), with parallel `HirError` variants added to validate.rs only where validate.rs actually runs the check (e.g. aggregate byte cap at validate.rs:507). The spec's `HirError::` labels for typecheck-phase checks are imprecise (warning #2).
positives_verified: MED-1 FIX genuinely bidirectional in spec text: §8 explicitly mandates 'register_shared MUST be EXTENDED to reject a name already present in the local-array name map' — the exact side a lazy mirror would skip. Verified against register_shared (typecheck.rs:812-843), which today checks ONLY shared_name_map + find_param + find_binding and is blind to local arrays. The fix is correctly targeted and order-independent. AT-2942 covers both orders.

MED-2 FIX mechanically feasible and cheap: typecheck has TWO distinct statement-dispatch paths — top-level (typecheck.rs:1197 handles SharedDecl) and nested-block (typecheck.rs:1795 handles SharedDecl). The nested path can emit LocalArrayDeclNotAtBlockScope while the top-level path registers — no new nesting-depth counter needed, the structural split already exists. Confirms the ~10 LOC estimate.

Const-OOB boundary is EXACT: §5.2 rejects a constant literal index >= N (valid range 0..=N-1), symbolic exempt; U32 index type precludes negatives. AT-2944 covers h[8] on array[u32,8] (reject), 0..=N-1 (clean), symbolic (clean). No off-by-one in the boundary spec.

Golden-identity re-confirmed inert: grep of examples/ shows `array` occurs ONLY inside // comments (flash_attention.axc:46/70, matmul_rb_coopmat.axc:14/19, matmul_shared_coopmat.axc:32/33, et al.), which the lexer strips pre-tokenization — zero bare-identifier or field-key use. AT-2940 corpus-wide byte-identity is safe by construction.

Schema v3->v4 factual fix verified: CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION=4 at metadata.rs:194; the test at metadata.rs:434 asserts the M3.17 bump. AT-2939/2941 corrected to v4. Local arrays remain metadata-inert (shared_memory_bytes==0, no field, no bump) — golden-friendly.
token.rs file-correction accurate: keyword_from_str at token.rs:234 with "shared"=>Some(TokenKind::Shared) at token.rs:256; lib.rs only re-exports. The spec's §12 line citations are correct.

LOC reconciliation honest and anchored: verified shared.rs hir=191, codegen=223 (the two new-module anchors). §12's math (optimistic ~2745 comparable minus ~700 barrier-hazard proof M3.20 omits = ~2045 cap -> 2000; target 1600) is defensible and the table explicitly retracts r1's 800 as a planning failure. The Coder is told overage toward 2000 is expected and must be self-reported (M3.18/M3.19 precedent).
AT range collision-free: AT-2927..AT-2944 appear only in M3.20 files; prior campaign tops at AT-2926; AT-2945 is cited solely as the budget ceiling. 18 ATs, within budget.

Path-insensitivity now honestly disclosed (§5): the write-set is a source-order presence set, zero-false-positive but misses true positives (write-in-if masks else-read; zero-trip loop) — stated in both directions, matching shared's SET-based conservatism. Forward-compat array-as-field-key narrowing (§15) and M3.12-as-analogy reframing (§15) also applied.

OpPhi non-interaction re-affirmed: Function-storage arrays are memory (OpVariable + OpLoad/OpStore); AT-2938 proves loop-carried array accumulation needs no OpPhi. Correct against M3.3 (only opaque coopmat SSA needs OpPhi).
